title: traffic-harmonizer-session-coherent-mini-rehearsals-with-adaptive-backpressure
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces Session Harmonizer and mini-rehearsal lanes for safer, lower-latency canary promotions. No consumer API breakage. Admins can opt-in via rollout policy flags.
description:
Motivation: Large-scale model swaps frequently cause transient regressions that are amplified by session-splitting (sticky sessions) and bursty load patterns. Existing staged-rollout controllers handle fractioned traffic but do not coordinate session-coherence during rehearsals, which leads to noisy SLO signals and difficult-to-reproduce failures. This PR introduces the 'Traffic Harmonizer' subsystem: a set of lightweight, session-aware mini-rehearsal lanes with adaptive backpressure that run pre-promote rehearsals on a bounded, session-coherent cohort to detect session-affecting regressions earlier and reduce noise from cross-session bleed.

Summary of changes: Added a new rollout controller component (session_harmonizer) and orchestration helpers for mini-rehearsal lanes, plus: 1) an agent to pin session cookies/headers for rehearsal cohorts, 2) an adaptive backpressure algorithm that slows promotion when per-session error or latency variance exceeds thresholds, 3) a drain-and-replay shadow path for session-affine traffic to validate stateful behavior without impacting main cohorts, 4) rollout policy schema extensions to opt into harmonized rehearsals and configure cohort size, warmup windows, and backpressure sensitivity.

Key behaviors and defaults: - Default mini-rehearsal cohort: 0.5% of global traffic or 1k sessions (whichever smaller) for the first 10 minutes. - Warmup: ephemeral KV cache priming for rehearsal lanes for 2 minutes to avoid cold-cache artifacts. - Backpressure: multiplicative reduction of inbound rehearsal fraction on sustained 95th-p99 latency deviation > 30% or error-rate spike > 2x baseline for 2 consecutive evaluation intervals. - Fallback: if harmonized rehearsal fails or stalls, traffic is routed to the stable model and the harmonizer auto-aborts; operators receive a high-priority alert with a replay snapshot.

Why this is different: Rather than increasing global canary fraction or relying on long-running shadows, harmonized mini-rehearsals constrain risk by (a) keeping sessions intact during rehearsal so stateful regressions surface, (b) adaptively throttling rehearsal traffic to avoid cascading failures, and (c) capturing short session replays for deterministic post-mortem.

Implementation notes (commits summary): - commit 1: core controller scaffolding and CRD extensions (session_harmonizer controller, policy API). - commit 2: session pinning agent and header propagation for rehearsal lanes. - commit 3: adaptive backpressure algorithm and metrics (percentile deltas, session-variance counters). - commit 4: shadow drain + deterministic replay buffer implementation. - commit 5: unit + integration tests and rollout policy docs.

Files changed (high level): - orchestration/controller/session_harmonizer.go (new) - orchestration/api/rollout_policy.proto (schema extension) - agents/session_pin/agent.py (new) - runtime/routing/harmonizer_router.cc (routing/backpressure logic) - telemetry/metrics/harmonizer_metrics.yaml (new metrics and dashboards) - docs/rollouts/session_harmonizer.md (operator guide) - tests/integration/test_harmonizer_rehearsal.py (integration tests)

Compatibility and migrations: - Rollout policy schema is backward compatible; fields are optional and default to disabled. - No customer-facing API changes to the Redwood REST generation endpoints; this is an orchestration-level enhancement. - Operators wishing to enable harmonized rehearsals must add a single flag to their rollout policy and optionally set cohort sizing.

Testing and CI: - Unit coverage: controller logic, backpressure math, and agent header flows. - Integration cluster test: rehearsals executed against a shadow model with simulated stateful sessions; validated that replay buffer captured deterministic flows and that harmonizer aborted on induced latency spikes. - Load tests: verified that adaptive backpressure throttles rehearsal traffic under sustained error injection and that stable traffic remained unaffected. - CI: build / unit / integration matrix passed on Linux and macOS runners; flakey test fixed in a follow-up commit.

Review conversation (high level): - Liam O'Neill: "Can we avoid adding a second cache priming path? I worry about duplication with the KV prewarmers we already have." Author reply: "We reuse the existing KV prewarm interfaces; session_harmonizer adds only a short-lived priming window orchestration layer — addressed by refactor in commit 3 to call prewarm service." - Priya Desai: "Need clearer operator visibility when harmonizer aborts; add an explicit reason in the alert." Author: "Added harmonizer.abort_reason tag and dashboard panel; see telemetry change." - Santiago Ruiz: "Backpressure tuning will likely need per-customer knobs — can we expose sensitivity in rollout policy?" Author: "Yes, added 'backpressure_sensitivity' and 'max_rehearsal_fraction' fields; documented defaults." - Code owner approvals: Liam and Priya approved after 2 iterations.

CI timeline: - First CI run: integration failed due to race in replay buffer; fix applied in commit 4. - Second CI run: all checks passed (unit+integration+lint). - E2E: running flagged as unstable in nightly; tracked as follow-up ENG-2034 to stabilize with longer warmup for very high cache-churn workloads.

Metrics and observability added: - harmonizer.rehearsal_fraction - harmonizer.session_variance_p95 - harmonizer.abort_reason - harmonizer.replay_buffer_size - rollout.harmonizer_backpressure_events - Dashboard panels: rehearsal overview, session variance heatmap, backpressure events timeline.

Operational playbook (short): - Enabling: flip rollout_policy.harmonizer.enabled = true, optionally set cohort_size and backpressure_sensitivity. - Monitoring: watch harmonizer.session_variance_p95 and backpressure events; aborts generate an alert with replay snapshot link. - Rollback: harmonizer auto-aborts on severe regressions; manual revert of rollout policy will remove harmonizer lanes.

Follow-ups and open questions: - ENG-2034: stabilize harmonizer under extreme cache-churn (nightly test failures). - Consider adding synthetic session generator to exercise rehearsal lanes for low-traffic tenants. - Evaluate telemetry retention policy for replay buffers.

Merge: squash and merge performed by Priya Desai on 2026-02-20. No post-merge hotfix required.

References: Linear ENG-1987 (session-coherent rehearsals design), SUP-9142 (customer incident prompting session-aware validation), internal docs/arch/rollouts-notes.md.
notes: Squash merged; telemetry, docs, and controller changes live in main. Operators must opt in. Follow-up ENG-2034 opened for stabilization and test hardening.
